title_ar: الكلام على الوسوسة في الطهارة والصلاة وطرق علاجها
title_en: On Obsessive Whispering in Purification and Prayer, and How to Treat It
body_ar:
عندي ولد تأخذه الوسوسة في الطهارة و الصلاة فإذا ذهب إلى الخلاء و تطهر من البول يتوضأ حتى ينتهي فيقول أنا لم أخلص من البول و لا أقدر على أن أصلي بالنجاسة و ينزع لباسه كله و يأخذ لباسا آخر و يصلي؟

أن هذا النوع هو من عمل الشيطان و قد قال الله تعالى:﴿يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان﴾ فعليه أن يتعالج من هذا المرض بأسباب الشفاء الشرعية و منها الإكثار من الإستغفار و منها كذلك أذكار دخول الخلاء و الخروج منه و الحفاظ عليها و منها أيضا عدم إتعاب النفس في التفكير كثيرا في هذا الأمر فيجب عليه أن يصرفه عن نفسه و منها أيضا الرقية الشرعية أن يقرأ القرآن على نفسه و أن يقرأه عليه غيره و منها الحفاظ على أذكار النوم و الإستيقاظ و الصباح و المساء و منها الصدقة التي يعالج بها المرض «عالجوا مرضاكم بالصدقة» فكل ذلك يزيل عنه هذا الوسواس بإذن الله
body_en:
I have a son who is seized by obsessive whispering (waswasah) in purification (ṭahārah) and prayer. When he goes to the lavatory and cleans himself of urine, he performs ablution right through to the end, and then says: I have not got free of the urine, and I cannot pray with substantive impurity (najāsah) on me — and he takes off all his clothing, takes other clothing, and prays.

This kind of thing is from the work of Satan. God, exalted, has said: {O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21). So he must treat himself for this illness with the means of healing given in the revealed law. Among them: frequent seeking of forgiveness. Among them likewise: the remembrances for entering the lavatory and for leaving it, and keeping to them. Among them also: not wearying himself by thinking much about this matter — he is obliged to turn it away from himself. Among them also: the lawful incantation (ruqyah), that he recite the Qur'an over himself and that someone else recite it over him. Among them: keeping to the remembrances for sleeping and waking, and for morning and evening. And among them: the voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) by which illness is treated — 'Treat your sick with charity.' All of that will remove this obsessive whispering from him, by God's leave.

flags.context: عندي ولد تأخذه الوسوسة في الطهارة و الصلاة … فكل ذلك يزيل عنه هذا الوسواس بإذن الله
options: compulsive doubt in matters of worship (waswasah)
flags.note: waswasah covers both the satanic insinuation and the sufferer's compulsive doubt, and the Sheikh's answer works on both levels at once: he names it 'the work of Satan' and also calls it 'this illness' to be treated. Option 2 keeps only the first sense and option 1 only the second. Note also that the Sheikh prescribes only religious remedies here; he neither recommends nor rules out medical treatment, and nothing on that has been added.

flags.context: و منها الصدقة التي يعالج بها المرض «عالجوا مرضاكم بالصدقة»
options: quote as the Sheikh gives it, with no grading
quote and mark it as a report whose grading is disputed
render as a general maxim rather than a quotation
flags.note: The Sheikh gives this in quotation marks as a report but names no narrator, no collection and no grading. None has been supplied. The grading of this particular report is contested in the hadith literature, so a reviewer may wish the site to say that the Sheikh gives none.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The question ends with a question mark in the source although it is phrased as a statement; the punctuation has been kept in the Arabic and the English reads it as the question it is.

The Qur'anic quotation is given in the source without a reference; the reference has been supplied in the English per house style. The wording matches Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21; the same prohibition occurs at 2:168, 2:208 and 6:142 with different openings.
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: الإستغفار and الإستيقاظ, written with a connecting hamza.
